newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates, bonds idle in late trade, ecu/drs range.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates, bonds idle in late trade, ecu/drs range.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were holding midsession levels in late dealings, fixed coupon bonds were steady and ecu/drachma was locked in the 309.0-309.50 range, dealers said.

"It is very quiet in late trade and it looks as if interbank rates have found their equilibrium for now," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "It will be interesting to see what is going to happen on Monday when a large amount of funds leaves the system."
The state is going to collect about 350 billion drachmas from telecom OTE's recent part-flotation, he said.
The central bank might have to step in and inject liquidity into the market on Monday to contain a rise in interbank rates due to tighter liquidity conditions, dealers said.
Bonds were also taking their cues from interbank rates, idling in late dealings, bond dealers said.

"Bonds slid this morning but have held their ground since mid-session," said a senior bond trader at a private bank. "Players do not like high funding costs and bonds will be vulnerable bonds for as long as interbank rates remain at these levels."
Ecu/drachma was trading in narrow ranges in late dealings, locked in the 309.0/50 band despite a short-lived ecu spike linked to the purchase of about 60 billion yens for drachmas at the fixing.
"A foreign bank bought about 60 billion yens for drachmas at the fixing," said a forex dealer. "Ecu/drachma hit 309.50 after the fixing but eased afterwards to 309.23/38."

The purchase of yens for drachmas must be corporate linked, the dealer said. The mark was quoted at 158.02/12 from Friday's 158.060 fix, the dollar at 273.69/79 drachmas from 272.940 and the ecu at 309.33/43 from 309.250 drachmas.
